verses.sa: चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः । बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥
verses.tr: With your mind, surrender all actions to Me. Take refuge in the discipline of clear understanding and remain constantly focused on Me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now gives the inner method for that surrender, and you will hear the mind itself made into the offering.

body.text: With your mind, surrender all actions to Me. Take refuge in the discipline of clear understanding and remain constantly focused on Me. The verse asks Arjuna to use his mind to place every action into Me, then to take refuge in the discipline of clear understanding, and to keep the mind fixed on Me. Centered in me, you will cross all obstacles through my grace. But if you do not listen because of ego, you will fall.

verses.sa: मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि । अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ॥
verses.tr: Centered in me, you will cross all obstacles through my grace. But if you do not listen because of ego, you will fall.
verses.angle: Ahankarat: the ego that blocks hearing
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna sums up his teaching with a promise and a warning. Listen to the single word that names the real danger to Arjuna's peace.

body.text: Centered in me, you will cross all obstacles through my grace. But if you do not listen because of ego, you will fall. The word ahankarat, from ego, names the inner force that makes Arjuna turn away from listening and brings ruin. Next, Krishna continues.

verses.sa: यदहङ्कारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे । मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति ॥
verses.tr: Relying on ego, you think, 'I will not fight.' That resolve is false; your nature will drive you into battle.
verses.angle: Ego as the false ground of Arjuna's resolve
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna strips away Arjuna’s final excuse to stay still. Listen for the word that names the pride behind this refusal.

body.text: Relying on ego, you think, 'I will not fight.' That resolve is false; your nature will drive you into battle. Arjuna's vow 'I will not fight' rests on ego, Krishna says, and his own nature will overrule it. Krishna then says that Arjuna is bound by his own nature-born duty, and will act even against his own will.

verses.sa: स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा । कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत् ॥
verses.tr: Bound by your own nature-born duty, you will do what you do not want to do in confusion. Even against your will, you will act.
verses.angle: Svabhava: your own nature drives you
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to one word that will shape the rest of this chapter. Listen for what your own nature demands of you.

body.text: Bound by your own nature-born duty, you will do what you do not want to do in confusion. Even against your will, you will act. The word svabhava, your own nature, is the engine here. It tells Arjuna that his own blood and upbringing are already pushing him toward action, so his current refusal is only a surface hesitation. Krishna now says the Lord sits in every heart and uses maya to make beings spin according to their nature.

verses.sa: ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति । भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥
verses.tr: O Arjuna, the Lord abides in the heart of all beings and, by His maya, causes all beings mounted on a body-machine to revolve according to their nature.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna that his own nature will force him to fight. Now Krishna reveals the deeper force behind all action: the Lord inside every heart, turning the body-machine by maya.

body.text: O Arjuna, the Lord abides in the heart of all beings and, by His maya, causes all beings mounted on a body-machine to revolve according to their nature. The Lord sits in every being's heart, Krishna says, turning them by maya as if mounted on a machine. Krishna then tells Arjuna to surrender his whole being to this divine, so he can reach supreme peace and the eternal abode.

verses.sa: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत । तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥
verses.tr: Surrender to the divine with your whole being, Arjuna. By that grace, you will reach supreme peace and the eternal abode.
verses.angle: Sharanam, refuge, shifts the burden from the self
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just shown him the hidden order behind all action and thought. Now he offers a final turn, a way to end the struggle.

body.text: Surrender to the divine with your whole being, Arjuna. By that grace, you will reach supreme peace and the eternal abode. The word refuge, sharanam, marks the final shift. It tells Arjuna to stop carrying the weight of the world and to place the burden entirely on the divine. Krishna steps back, telling Arjuna to reflect on this secret wisdom and then choose his own path.

verses.sa: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया । विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
verses.tr: Thus I have explained to you the most secret wisdom. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish.
verses.angle: Krishna hands the choice back to Arjuna
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: After revealing the deepest secret, Krishna steps back and asks Arjuna to decide for himself. Listen for the moment he hands the choice back.

body.text: Thus I have explained to you the most secret wisdom. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish. Krishna tells Arjuna to think this over completely, then act as he wishes. He gives Arjuna the freedom to choose and act for himself. Krishna now calls Arjuna dear to him, and says he will speak one last secret word for his good.

verses.sa: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥
verses.tr: Listen again to My most secret word. You are dear to Me, so I will speak for your good.
verses.angle: Isthah asi: because you are dear
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna to reflect on the secret wisdom and then choose his own path. Now he asks him to listen once more.

body.text: Listen again to My most secret word. You are dear to Me, so I will speak for your good. Krishna names the reason for his final command: Arjuna is dear to him, and therefore he will speak only what is truly good for him. Because Arjuna is dear to him, Krishna now gives the final command to fix his mind on him.

verses.sa: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु । मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥
verses.tr: Fix your mind on me, become my devotee, worship me, and bow to me. You will come to me; I promise you this truly, because you are dear to me.
verses.angle: Manmana bhava: the mind Krishna asks for
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now offers the simplest path. Listen for the instruction to fix the mind on Him.

body.text: Fix your mind on me, become my devotee, worship me, and bow to me. You will come to me; I promise you this truly, because you are dear to me. The key phrase is manmana bhava, with mind on me. Krishna asks for nothing but a focused mind, and in return promises that you will come to me alone. He seals this with his reason: you are dear to me.

verses.sa: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज । अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥
verses.tr: Abandon all duties and take refuge in Me alone. I will free you from all wrongdoing; do not grieve.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just promised his love. Now he gives the final command that closes the entire dialogue. Listen for the one instruction that asks for everything.

body.text: Abandon all duties and take refuge in Me alone. I will free you from all wrongdoing; do not grieve. Listen for sarva-dharman parityajya, having abandoned all duties. Krishna asks Arjuna to drop every other support, every other path, and take refuge in Me alone. Krishna then warns Arjuna never to speak this teaching to the faithless or the fault-finding.

verses.sa: इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन । न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति ॥
verses.tr: Never speak this to one without discipline, one without devotion, one unwilling to listen, or one who finds fault with me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna to abandon all duties and take refuge in Him, and now He places a condition on the teaching itself.

body.text: Never speak this to one without discipline, one without devotion, one unwilling to listen, or one who finds fault with me. The word anashushrushave, to one unwilling to listen, is the sharpest warning. After revealing the deepest secret, Krishna refuses to let it reach a closed mind. He then turns to the one who does share it, promising that they will come to Him without doubt.

verses.sa: य इमं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति । भक्ितं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः ॥
verses.tr: Whoever shares this supreme secret among my devotees, with devoted love for me, will surely come to me without doubt.
verses.angle: The secret is for devotees only
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just finished his final instruction, but he adds one more condition about who may hear it. Listen to that boundary.

body.text: Whoever shares this supreme secret among my devotees, with devoted love for me, will surely come to me without doubt. The secret is not for everyone, but for those who already love Krishna. The word asamsayah, without doubt, seals the promise: anyone who teaches it with supreme devotion will come to me. Krishna then promises that no one on earth is more dear to him than the one who shares this secret.

verses.sa: न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्िचन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः । भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि ॥
verses.tr: Among all human beings, no one does what is more dear to me than he does. On this earth, no one will ever be dearer than he is.
verses.angle: priyakarittamah, the one who does the most dear service
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna closes the dialogue with a final promise. Listen to how he names the person who will be dearest to him.

body.text: Among all human beings, no one does what is more dear to me than he does. On this earth, no one will ever be dearer than he is. Listen to priyakarittamah. It means the one who does the most dear service. This is the person who teaches the teaching, and Krishna places him above all others on earth. Krishna now says that the one who studies this dialogue will also worship him through the sacrifice of knowledge.

verses.sa: अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः । ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः ॥
verses.tr: Whoever studies this sacred dialogue of ours will also worship me through the sacrifice of knowledge; that is my view.
verses.angle: Jnana yajna, a sacrifice of knowledge
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for the word yajna. You might expect a blood sacrifice or a fire offering, but Krishna names a very different kind of offering.

body.text: Whoever studies this sacred dialogue of ours will also worship me through the sacrifice of knowledge; that is my view. Yajna is a sacrifice, and Krishna calls the study of this dialogue a jnana yajna, a sacrifice of knowledge. He says that anyone who reads these words is worshipping him directly. Krishna then says that even listening to this dialogue with trust frees a person from evil and leads to heaven.
